sections.history: Tiruanniyur lies in the Kudavasal taluk of Tiruvarur district, among the Shiva shrines of the southern bank of the Kaveri. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, revered in the Tevaram hymns. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later, keeping the form of the delta shrines. Two Tevaram temples bear the name Tiru-Anniyur; this is the Agneeswarar shrine of the south, distinct from the northern Anniyur dedicated to Aabathsahayeswarar.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Agneeswarar in the sanctum, with the Goddess in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. The walled courtyard and modest gopuram are typical of the Shiva temples of the Kudavasal country.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Agneeswarar, the name recalling the devotion of Agni, the god of fire, among the delta shrines. The Goddess stands beside him; local tradition also gives her the name Karpagambikai, though the sources vary. As with many delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives chiefly in local tradition and the Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims of the Kudavasal country include Tiruanniyur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruanniyur the pilgrim comes to a quiet shrine of the fire-god's lord. Before Agneeswarar and the Goddess, in the green Kudavasal country of the Tiruvarur delta, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the southern Kaveri.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruanniyur lies in the Kudavasal taluk of Tiruvarur district, in the southern Kaveri delta. Kudavasal and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
